TITLE: Investigating Calibration of Time Series Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Compare the calibration properties of a global TSFM (using GPT-FTS) trained on a diverse set of time series from various domains (including online review activity forecasting, retail sales forecasting, and crime report forecasting) against a suite of baseline methods (including ARIMA, N-BEATS, and Informer) on two real-world metrics: Brier score (a strict probabilistic calibration metric) and event-level calibration plots (visualizing the probability of a specific event vs. its observed frequency).
CONTROLS: Baseline models' calibration will be evaluated without adaptation; all tested models will use the same frequentist evaluation metrics.
COST: 5000 GPU-hours (combining forecast errors and re-computing various statistics for calibration)
PREDICTION: TSFMs will show moderate improvement in Brier score over baseline methods due to their global scope, but may fail to significantly outperform baselines in event-level calibration plots due to aggregation-related issues, presence of structural breaks, or differential-DGP calibration among individual time series.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Evaluating the Effect of Forecast Horizon on Calibration in Time Series Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment to investigate how the choice of forecast horizon affects the calibration of TSFMs on long-term forecasts. We will train five different TSFM models (Prophet, RepeatFormer, Temporal Fusion Transformer, LiDenseNet, and Conv-TASNET) on a dataset of diverse real-world time series and evaluate their calibration using the CRPS, WQL, and MSIS metrics for varying forecast horizons (1-day, 1-week, 1-month, and 3-month) in the domains of online review activity forecasting, retail sales forecasting, and crime report forecasting. 
CONTROLS: We will compare the results to those of the non-TSFM baselines (ARIMA and N-BEATS), and ablate the effect of using different TSFM models on calibration.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: We expect that TSFMs will be more calibrated on shorter-term forecasts, but their accuracy may degrade on longer-term forecasts, and that the effect of autoregressive scheme on calibration will be significant. The CRPS and WQL metrics may show underestimation on longer-term forecasts, but the MSIS metric may indicate consistent calibration across different horizons.

We will train three TSFM models (Prophet, RepeatFormer, and Temporal Fusion Transformer) with different prediction head forms (density model parameters and distribution predictions, e.g. quantiles) on a dataset of real-world time series from these domains, and evaluate their calibration using the CRPS, WQL, and MSIS metrics.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results to those of TSFMs with autoregressive prediction heads and ablate the effect of using unconditional models.

PREDICTION: We expect that TSFMs with heads predicting conditional density model parameters will be more calibrated than those predicting conditional quantiles, especially when evaluated with the CRPS and WQL metrics, and that TSFMs with autoregressive heads will show a mismatch between the predicted and observed frequencies.
